library_preparation_preflight.summary: opentelemetry-spring-boot-autoconfigure declares spring-boot-autoconfigure (and the rest of Spring Boot) as compileOnly; this is invisible to Gradle Module Metadata, so the generated scaffold cannot auto-resolve it. Without it, the @AutoConfiguration entry points cannot load, so coverage would be near zero. This mirrors the existing pattern in sibling modules (opentelemetry-spring-webmvc-5.3, -spring-web-3.1, -spring-webflux-5.3, -spring-kafka-2.7, -micrometer-1.5), each of which had its compileOnly peer framework added manually as testImplementation. No Docker image is required: the conditional sub-configurations (Kafka, Mongo, JDBC, R2DBC, Micrometer, WebMVC/WebFlux) only check for a class on the classpath, not a live connection, and upstream's own tests back the JDBC/R2DBC paths with in-memory H2 rather than containers.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Use the standard Spring Boot autoconfigure test idiom (ApplicationContextRunner / AutoConfigurations.of(OpenTelemetryAutoConfiguration.class, ...)) to exercise the conditional configuration classes without needing a full running application. The default OTLP exporter properties (otel.exporter.otlp.endpoint, protocol http/protobuf) are unset but still active by default, so a fully-wired OpenTelemetry bean may attempt background network export; set otel.sdk.disabled=true or otel.traces.exporter=none / otel.metrics.exporter=none / otel.logs.exporter=none as test properties to keep tests hermetic and avoid noisy export attempts. The nested auto-configurations for Kafka, Mongo, JDBC, R2DBC, Micrometer, WebMVC and WebFlux are each gated behind @ConditionalOnClass for their respective peer library (e.g. org.springframework.kafka:spring-kafka, io.micrometer:micrometer-core, org.springframework:spring-webmvc) — only add one of those as an additional test dependency if the test suite intends to exercise that specific integration; otherwise Spring Boot's conditional evaluation will harmlessly skip it.
risks: The jar also ships separate 'SpringBoot4'-suffixed auto-configuration classes (Kafka producer customizer, Mongo client, JDBC, Micrometer bridge, WebClient/RestClient) that only become eligible with Spring Boot 4.x on the classpath. Pairing with Spring Boot 3.2.4 as recommended will not exercise those classes; a follow-up pass pairing with Spring Boot 4.x would be needed to cover them, and may also change which of the non-suffixed classes remain active.

Upstream's own CI validates the shared/default code paths against Spring Boot 2.7.18 specifically (their compileOnly/testLibrary pin); 3.2.4 is a reasonable, currently-supported choice but has not been verified upstream bit-for-bit against every conditional branch.
